creaite design system

The definitive guide to how creaite looks and how to build a new page in it. Everything here is the real app: real markup, drawn by the app's own stylesheet, measured on the running screens. If this guide and the app disagree, the app is right and this guide has a fault: tell the Product Manager.

Taken from commit c237a088origin/v220-int-gate (VERSION file 2.1.0)2026-10-17palette creaite, light and dark; also checked in Cursordesktop and 900 px only

Build a page

For a mockup, and for the real thing. Seven steps; each is the whole rule.

  1. Choose the pattern.Pick the nearest of the page patterns in section 5 (a list, a tabbed list, a queue, a brief, a detail page, settings, a document, two panes, docs, cards). If none fits, say why in the write-up before drawing anything.
  2. Copy its snapshot.Quickest: copy a starter from templates/ (list, tabbed list, detail, settings). Otherwise, for a mockup copy pages/<pattern>.html (or blank.html) into dev/mockups/, change the stylesheet link to ../design-system/style.snapshot.css, and replace the content of the #v-… section only. Keep the rail and the top bar.
  3. Build the page in the standard order.<section class="view" id="v-name"><div class="wrapmax">, then (if a detail page) the .crumb, then h1, then .sub, then the control row (.toolbar), then the content (cards or a .tbl).
  4. Use the components as they are.Buttons 32 px, one primary per region; icon buttons labelled; view pills for views; the funnel for filters; dates as text with a calendar button; counts and Refresh at the right of the control row.
  5. Say what is empty, loading and wrong.Every list has an empty state that names the next step; an error says what happened and what to do; Undo accompanies every change that can be undone.
  6. Check keyboard, dark mode and words.Tab through it; Esc closes the top-most thing; it works in dark (Alt+D) and in creaite and Cursor; sentence case, British English, DD-MM-YYYY, project full names.
  7. Mark anything new.If you genuinely need a component that is not here, put it in one block marked /* NEW */, built from tokens only, and name it in the write-up so it can be added to this guide.

Wiring a new page into the app (for the build)

  1. Add the section in system/templates/dashboard/shell.html: <section class="view" id="v-name" hidden><div class="wrapmax">… (a page that draws itself leaves it empty and renders into it).
  2. Put the screen's code in src/<area>.js (or a component under src/components/<area>/, per dev/COMPONENTS.md): a render function that fills #v-name.
  3. Make go('name') show it: core/nav.js hides every .view and shows #v- + the name; give it a hash route in the same file (#name=…) so refresh, Back and links work.
  4. Add it to the side bar or More in src/stores/rail.js (RAIL_ITEMS) with an icon from the icon table (section 3) and, if it has a count, setRailCount.
  5. Register it in ⌘K if it is a place to jump to, and in Help (system/templates/help.md: a job and a Screen: line).
  6. Test it: the shared behaviour test (dev/tests/test_shared_behaviour.py) walks every menu, picker and dialog for keys and focus; add the page to the snapshots in dev/tests/snapshots/ and write its own tests.

Ten rules

  1. One primary button per region.
  2. Controls are the standard ones at their standard sizes.
  3. Colours are tokens only; it must work in dark and in every palette.
  4. Spacing, sizes, radii and layers come from the scale.
  5. Titles are display-font h1/h2; body is the text font; tables and labels use mono.
  6. Every list has an empty state; every change has Undo or a clear way back.
  7. Filters live in the funnel; views are pills; kinds are tabs.
  8. Dates are text with a calendar button, DD-MM-YYYY.
  9. Icons come from the app's icon table, always labelled.
  10. Nothing is shown that is not true; nothing changes without a visible way to undo.

Foundations

Tokens only; never a raw hex. Each shows its light and dark value, its job, and how many rules in the stylesheet use it.

Type

Families

  • Text: "Source Sans 3","Segoe UI",system-ui,-apple-system,Arial,sans-serif
  • Display (h1, h2, h3): "Schibsted Grotesk","Helvetica Neue",Arial,sans-serif
  • Mono (table headers, key hints, small labels): "JetBrains Mono",ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,monospace

h1 weight 800 with −0.02em; h2 and h3 weight 700. Table headers: mono 12 px, weight 500, uppercase, letter-spaced .08em (the creaite palette's own rule).

Icons (82)

The app's own icon table. 24 px grid, 1.8 px round-cap stroke, currentColor. Click one to copy its name. The sparkle (spark) is the AI mark.

Palettes: creaite and Cursor

Two palettes are tested in every release (creaite, the default, and Cursor). A page must work in both, light and dark. A palette changes colours, fonts and a few shapes; never the layout. Use the toggle at the left to see this whole guide in each.

Tokencreaite lightcreaite darkCursor lightCursor dark
--bg #F3F6F7 #0F1518 #F7F7F4 #1A1915
--surface #FFFFFF #171E22 #FFFFFF #23221D
--sunk #EAF0F2 #1E272C #EFEEE8 #2C2B25

Cursor draws the accent as orange, the page on warm paper, and its shadows as a hairline ring; its type is its own gothic with Inter behind it. creaite is teal on cool grey with Source Sans 3, Schibsted Grotesk and JetBrains Mono. The other seven palettes exist but are not tested.

The app shell

Every page lives inside the same frame. Never redraw it.

Anatomy

  • Side bar (.rail): 224px wide expanded (--rail-w), 56 px icons only, 76 px icons with labels; items 36 px; Today first, More at the foot.
  • Top bar (.bar): 53 px; search or jump (⌘K) at the left, ask creaite and the theme switch at the right.
  • Page (.view): padding 20 × 24 × 40 px on the page tint; content in .wrapmax, max 1500 px.
  • Peek (#panel.peek): over the right half, at least 520 px, 50% of the window.
  • ask creaite panel opens over the page, never squeezing it.

The real frame

Every snapshot in pages/ carries it. Start from blank.html.

Components

Each specimen is the app's own markup, drawn by its own stylesheet. The state pictures are the real component with the state forced (hover, focus, active, disabled), in light and dark.

Headings and text

h1 · h2 · h3 · .sub

h1 titles a page; h2 titles a card or a section; h3 titles a block inside one; .sub is the muted line beneath a title.

For example: risks ABC last month, or what did Sara say about UAT?

Button

.btn (.primary, .quiet)

.btn is the standard action. .btn.primary is the one main action in a region (an accent fill; Approve, Add, Run). .btn.quiet is a text-style action with no border (accent text, soft fill on hover).

Markup (real, to copy)
<div class="ds-row"><figure class="ds-cell"><button class="btn" id="filesRefresh">Refresh</button><figcaption>.btn</figcaption></figure><figure class="ds-cell"><button type="button" class="btn sm primary" id="wrApprove">Approve and file</button><figcaption>.btn.primary</figcaption></figure><figure class="ds-cell"><button class="btn quiet" id="filesRefresh">Refresh</button><figcaption>.btn.quiet</figcaption></figure></div>

Measured: button 68 × 32 px · text 13px/500 · radius 8px · padding 0px 12px · primary 116 × 32 px · text 13px/500 · radius 8px · padding 0px 12px

Not for: two primaries side by side, or a primary for something that is not the main thing here.

Icon button

.ib (.sm, .bd)

A button that is only an icon. Always has an aria-label and a data-tip tooltip. .sm only makes the icon 16 px; .bd draws a border (use it in a control row, like the funnel).

Tag, chip, count, file type, key hint

.tag · .chip · .fchip · .badge · .ftype · kbd

Small labels. .tag is plain muted text by default (a status word); .chip is a small pill; .fchip is a removable filter; .badge is the rail's count only (it only draws inside the side bar: see the side-bar item below); .ftype marks a file kind; kbd shows a key.

Markup (real, to copy)
<div class="ds-row"><figure class="ds-cell"><span class="tag stale">4 stale</span><figcaption>.tag</figcaption></figure><figure class="ds-cell"><span class="chip plan">this week</span><figcaption>.chip</figcaption></figure><figure class="ds-cell"><span class="fchip">Status: Open<button data-clr="st" aria-label="Remove the status filter" data-tip="Remove the status filter"><svg class="i" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" data-icn="x"><path d="M18 6 6 18M6 6l12 12"></path></svg></button></span><figcaption>.fchip</figcaption></figure><figure class="ds-cell"><span class="ftype">docx</span><figcaption>.ftype</figcaption></figure><figure class="ds-cell"><kbd id="kK">⌘K</kbd><figcaption>kbd</figcaption></figure></div>

Field error

.dwrap + its message

A mistake in a typed date is shown at the field, in the error colour, with the format it expects; nothing is saved from it.

Markup (real, to copy)

Date field

.dwrap + the popup calendar

Every date is a text field in DD-MM-YYYY with a calendar button; the button opens the popup calendar (below). Dates can also be typed in words in some fields.

Check box, switch, setting row

input[type=checkbox] · .switch · .srow

A check box is one of several; a switch is on or off right now. A setting row puts its label and one line of help at the left, its control at the right.

Your nameSet at first start. creaite uses it to know which items are yours.

Folder list

Floating and modal components (live screenshots)

Dropdown menu

.ddmenu

A list of choices under the control that opened it. Closes on Esc, a pick or a click outside.

Filter panel

.ddmenu.fpmenu

A larger menu for adding a filter: pick a field, then a value. Opened by the funnel.

Popup calendar

.cal

A month grid under a date field: today ringed, weekends marked, arrows for months.

Toast

#snack (.mtimer)

Says what just happened, with Undo when it can be undone. Stays 10 seconds with Undo (5 otherwise) and waits while you point at it.

Peek

#panel.peek

An item opens over the right half of the page, editable in place. ⌘↵ saves and closes; Esc closes.

Dialog (Customise sidebar)

dialog

A centred card on a scrim for a short, self-contained job. Cancel and the one main action at the foot; Reset at the left when it applies.

Command palette

#cmdk

⌘K: search, jump, and run commands.

ask creaite panel

#chat

The assistant opens over the page on the right and never squeezes it. Esc closes the panel but never stops a running request; only Stop stops it.

ask creaite while it works

#chat

A request in progress: the question, a folded step line ("1 step"), and a typing indicator while the answer arrives. Stop appears while it runs; Esc closes the panel but never stops the request.

AI suggestion card

.sheet-redraft

A ✦ draft under the section it is for: the sparkle and a title, the suggested text, amber warnings from the check (what it leaves out, what it adds, what has no source), the source facts as outlined boxes, then Keep mine and Use this. Nothing changes until Use this. (The words in this picture come from the test stand-in, not a real model.)

Error banner

.errbanner

Under the other page banners: how many errors, what kind, Investigate (opens Settings › Diagnostics), ask creaite to look, and a ✕ that dismisses it until a newer error. Shown only for an error not yet seen.

Live-server alert

#liveAlert.on

Shown at the top of every page when the live server is not running: what is held, and how to restart it.

Dialog (small)

dialog

A short question with its answer buttons.

Dialog (large)

dialog

A larger job with settings and a result (Generate current state).

Dialog (form)

dialog

A form in a dialog: fields, then Cancel and the main action.

Composite pieces (live screenshots)

Filter bar

Work: .toolbar + .views + .wapplied

Search, filter buttons, the funnel with its count, the layout switch and Display, the + button; then the view pills; then the applied filters as chips with Clear all and the count.

Queue group

Review: .rgroup + .tbl

A group header (check box, name, count, how many are stale) over a card of rows that each carry their facts in muted lines and the same row actions.

Rows of work

Work: .tbl.list

A work row is two lines: the title with a state box, then the ID (a dotted link) and the project in muted text. The owner is a dotted link (You for the current user); the due date is red with "n days late" when it is late, otherwise plain with "In n days"; urgent priority is red.

Day band

Today: .dayband .bandin

A mono date line, a display greeting, one sentence of what matters, and the calendar controls, on the day tint.

Numbered section

Today: .tsec (h2.th + ol.bl)

A display h2 with its count, then numbered one-sentence rows with their tools at the right.

Settings group

.card + .srow

A card with a display title and rows: label and one line of help at the left, the control at the right.

Health card

cockpit: .card

The health label (icon, word, colour), its six-week trend with a ? key, and the four figures that explain it.

Timeline card

cockpit and Milestones: .card

A month strip with Today marked; the plan as shapes on a line.

Page head with breadcrumb

.crumb + h1 + .sub

Where you are, what this is, and who it is for; a neighbour picker sits at the right.

Two panes

Notes

A labelled list with a search box and collapse chevron beside a card that reads or edits the item, or says what the thing is for.

Document view

Weekly report

Breadcrumb, title and sub; a bar with zoom and Show as exported at the left, Export and the one primary at the right; then the sheet on a tinted canvas.

Page patterns

Seventeen ways a creaite page is put together, in a handful of families (list, queue, brief, detail, settings, document, two panes, docs). Pick the nearest; do not invent another without saying why. Each links to the real screen and shows its skeleton from the running app.

List page: a heading, controls, a table card

open the real screen

Any page that is a list of things you search, filter and open: Files, People, Activity, Projects.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. h1 (display 22/800), no breadcrumb.
  2. Optional .sub line (13 px, muted).
  3. A control row (.toolbar, 32 px): search input, selects, date fields, a count and Refresh at the right.
  4. View pills (.vchip, 28 px) when the list has named views.
  5. The table in a .tbl card: mono uppercase headers, 14 px rows.

Rules

  • Content sits in .wrapmax (max 1500 px) inside the page's 20 × 24 px padding.
  • Counts and Refresh go to the right of the same row, never on a row of their own.
  • A row's one main action is its link; row tools are icon buttons at the end.
  • Empty: say the next step, in a .empty box inside the card.

Tabbed list with filters (Work)

open the real screen

A list that has kinds (Actions, RAID, Decisions) and many ways to narrow it.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. h1.
  2. .tabs for the kinds (38 px, an underline marks the selected one).
  3. The filter row: search, filter buttons (.btn.fbtn), the funnel (.ib.bd with its count) and view and layout icon buttons at the right.
  4. View pills (All open, Mine, Due soon …).
  5. Applied filters as removable chips with Clear all and the count ("Showing 3 of 3").
  6. The .tbl card.

Rules

  • The funnel icon button is how any list adds a filter: it carries the number of filters on.
  • Applied filters are always visible and removable one at a time.
  • Selected view pill = ink fill; the others are outlined.

Triage queue (Review)

open the real screen

A queue where each row needs one decision: approve, change, reject.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. h1 and a sub-line with the counts.
  2. Controls: search, toggles (One at a time, Kind, Needs, Source), funnel, display, the one bulk action at the right.
  3. Groups, each with a group check box, a name and a count.
  4. Rows in a card: check box, the thing, its facts in muted lines, per-row actions (project, edit, Approve, reject, expand).

Rules

  • Per-row actions are always the same set and in the same order.
  • The bulk action is named for exactly what it covers.
  • Facts that need attention are coloured (--warn), never bold.

Today: the brief

open the real screen

A page that reads like a briefing: what to know now, in short numbered sentences.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. A tinted day band (--day-band): mono date line, display greeting, one sentence of what matters, calendar controls.
  2. Numbered sections (Getting started, Needs attention, Your commitments, …): a display h2 with a count, then rows.
  3. Each row: number, one sentence, tools at the right (icon button and the ⋯ menu).

Rules

  • Content is a centred column, not the full width.
  • One sentence per row; the tools sit at the right and stay quiet until pointed at.

Detail page: breadcrumb, tabs, a grid of cards (Project)

open the real screen

One thing seen from several sides: a project, a person, a report space.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. Breadcrumb (.crumb), h1, a sub-line, a picker to jump to a neighbour at the right.
  2. Tabs (Overview, Notes).
  3. A grid of .cards (14 px padding, 12 px radius): the wide one first, then pairs.
  4. Each card: a display h2, its content, a quiet edit icon at the bottom right.

  • Health uses the health label (icon + word + colour), not colour alone.

A page you write, approve and export, shown as the paper it will become.

Composition, top to bottom

Rules

Two panes: a list and a reader (Notes)

open the real screen

Content you browse on the left and read or edit on the right.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. Breadcrumb, h1, a sub-line and a + button at the right.
  2. Tabs.
  3. Left: a labelled list with a search box and a collapse chevron. Right: a card with the content, or an empty state that says what the thing is for.

Rules

  • The empty state explains the thing in one sentence, then shows what to do.
  • The collapse control keeps its place.

  3. Cards, each one idea, with the one gate highlighted in --warn-soft.

Rules

  • Page-specific styles (Help has its own palette) stay inside the page.
  • Short sentences; one idea per card.

Sections of cards (Intake)

open the real screen

A page of separate jobs, each a card with its own action.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. h1 and a sub-line.
  2. A card per job (Calendar import, Upload files, Quick capture), each with a display title, its controls and its table.
  3. Empty states inside the card.

Rules

  • One primary button per card at most.
  • Controls repeat only if they do different things.

At 900 px wide
In the Cursor palette

Prep: three columns around one meeting

open the real screen

A working page for one thing you are about to do: a meeting.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. Breadcrumb, h1, a row of chips (kind, date and time, project, health, series position).
  2. Actions at the left (Refresh research, Draft agenda); the save note and Print at the right.
  3. Tabs (Prep, Invite, History).
  4. Three columns: an outline list at the left; the editors in the middle (mono labels, a ✦ Shape control, then "In play" rows with a Raise / Note / Skip switch); cards at the right (When and who, Latest reporting, This series).

Rules

  • The outline lists exactly what is on the page, in order.
  • Editors save as you type and say so ("Saved as you type").
  • Facts about other things come as cards at the side, never inline.

Document page, client version (Client report)

open the real screen

The same sheet pattern as the weekly report, seen as the client sees it.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. The same bar and sheet as the weekly report.
  2. Only client-visible items, in the client's words; what is left out is listed, with the reason, before any export.

Rules

  • Never anything marked Sensitive or partner-only.
  • The one primary action is still alone in the bar.

Document page with a side panel (Minutes)

open the real screen

The Document pattern when the sheet needs its source beside it.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. Breadcrumb, h1, a sub-line (project, date, status).
  2. A bar: zoom and Show as exported, an open-checks chip; then version, view switch, Transcript, Export and the one primary (Approve minutes).
  3. The sheet on its canvas; at the right a Transcript panel with its own search and the turns, each with a time tag that scrolls the transcript.

Rules

  • Time tags sit on the sheet's lines and link to the panel; the panel closes with its ✕.
  • A toast says what happened at the foot ("7 new items in Review").

Roll-up table across projects (Reports)

open the real screen

One row per project for a recurring job, with the state of each and an Open button.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. Breadcrumb, h1, a sub-line, and a week stepper at the right (a pair of ink-selected buttons).
  2. A tinted note that says what needs doing, with a two-way switch (Needs me | All projects).
  3. A .tbl of projects: health, internal state as a chip, client state as a chip, and Open (primary on the row that needs you).

Rules

  • State is a chip (Due, Not drafted, Filed), never colour alone.
  • The note under the table says what Open does.

A space for one thing over time (Reporting)

open the real screen

Everything about one project's reporting: a list of weeks and the two reports for the chosen week.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. Breadcrumb, h1, a sub-line.
  2. Left: a stack of week cards (the chosen one outlined), each with its state chips.
  3. Right: two cards (Weekly report, Client report) each with a preview, two facts and its actions; then a tinted call-to-action strip; then a card for what was filed.

Rules

  • Only the next sensible action is primary; the rest are plain; a blocked one says why ("Approve the internal report first").
  • A dashed tinted strip offers the combined action.

Detail page: a person (People)

open the real screen

Everything a person has with you: their work, what closed lately, decisions they made.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. Breadcrumb, h1, a sub-line; actions at the right (Draft email, Hand over, an edit icon).
  2. A one-line summary of figures (open actions, open risks and issues, overdue, projects).
  3. Cards, each with a display title and a count: Open work (with its own .tbl), Closed in the last 14 days, Decisions made.

Rules

  • An empty card says so in one plain line ("Nothing closed lately.").
  • Counts are in the title, not in a badge.

A single-purpose view with a switch (Milestones)

open the real screen

One visual thing with two ways of looking at it (Plan | Movement) and an Internal | Client view.

Composition, top to bottom

  1. Breadcrumb, h1, a project picker and the one primary (Add milestone) at the right.
  2. Two .seg switches.
  3. A card holding the plan: a month strip with Today marked.

Rules

  • The client view is the plain card: no pills or notes.
  • The Add button is the only primary.

States every page has

  • Empty: the .empty box (components) says what is missing and the next step.
  • Offline: the live-server alert above, on every page.
  • Loading: the stylesheet has no spinner or skeleton component (checked); a long job shows as steps in the ask creaite panel, or a .prog bar. Do not invent one.
  • Error: an error banner (.errbanner) under the page banners, dismissible; a failed save says what to do.

The minutes view is not snapshotted (it opens from a staged meeting's Open draft in Review); it follows the Document pattern: a sheet on a tinted canvas with a bar above it, the transcript beside the draft.

Interaction

Keys

⌘Kthe command palette: search, jump to a place, run a command
⌘Jopen or close ask creaite
/open ask creaite (when you are not typing)
?Help
Fadd a filter (Work)
Dthe Display menu (Work)
⌘↵save and close an editor or a dialog
Escclose the top-most thing: a menu or popup before the dialog or peek under it; it never stops a running request
Alt + ↑ ↓ ← →move a row or a section (side bar dialog, report sections)
⌘⇧Na note from anywhere
Tab / Shift+Tabevery control is reachable in reading order

The one hover standard

Tooltipopens after 400 ms, closes 150 ms after leaving; the next one opens after 100 ms
Card (a peek, the meeting-title popup)opens after 600 ms, closes 300 ms after leaving the trigger and the card
Menu (flyouts, toolbar groups)opens after 200 ms, closes after 300 ms; a neighbouring menu opens after 80 ms; a diagonal move toward the menu keeps it open

From src/core/hover.js. Keyboard focus opens a tooltip or card with no delay; Esc dismisses it and it stays shut until the pointer leaves.

  • Changes made in the page show at once and save in the background; an Undo toast follows anything undoable (10 seconds with Undo, 5 otherwise, and it waits while you point at it).
  • Anything that writes to the record waits for an approval; what creaite suggests always waits in Review.
  • Esc closes the top-most layer first (a menu or popup before the dialog or peek under it); it never stops a running request.

Words

  • British English, plain and short; sentence case for headings and buttons.
  • Dates on screen are DD-MM-YYYY (Today's day band writes them out: "Thursday 15th October"). Times are 24-hour.
  • A project is called by its full name; the short code appears only inside an item ID (ABC-A-003) and where a code is typed.
  • Name things by the job: Approve, Reject with a reason, Not needed, Later, Undo. Not Submit, Dismiss, OK.
  • Never call a person a VIP in anything creaite shows or writes; the word lives only in the person's own field and Settings.
  • Say what happened and what to do next. No developer words (a script name, "cx-edit", "inbox" for Intake).
  • A toast says what changed; an error says what failed and how to fix it.

Accessibility

  • Every icon button has an aria-label; every toggle has aria-pressed or aria-checked; the current page has aria-current="page".
  • Targets are at least 24 × 24 px, or have room around them.
  • The focus ring is :focus-visible in --focus; never remove it.
  • Colour is never the only signal: health and state use an icon and a word as well.
  • Reduced motion removes slides and fades; the delays stay the same. --k scales every duration.
  • Hover popups follow the one hover standard (below); the keyboard opens them with no delay and Esc dismisses them.

Checklist before a page or a mockup is shown

  1. Started from a snapshot or blank.html, linking the stylesheet copy; the file says which commit it came from.
  2. Every existing control is an existing class at its real size.
  3. One primary button per region; icon buttons labelled; filters in the funnel; views as pills.
  4. Colours and sizes are tokens; it works in dark and in creaite and Cursor.
  5. Empty, loading and error states are drawn; Undo is there for anything undoable.
  6. Keyboard: Tab order, Esc, ⌘↵ where it saves.
  7. Words: British English, sentence case, DD-MM-YYYY, project full names, no jargon.
  8. Anything genuinely new is in one /* NEW */ block and named in the write-up.
  9. Fictional data only; no real names.

Rough edges (do not copy)

On this line: font sizes have 19 distinct raw values, border radii 13, layers 10 raw uses in 7 values, line heights 22 distinct with no tokens, 49 distinct raw heights (Team Stark's recount, 17-10-2026). Controls come in more than one size by context (section 4); page titles are 34 px on Today and Help and 22 px elsewhere; .fsel is dead CSS (a 36 px, 16 px radius select no screen uses): do not copy it. #193 (tokens-193-full) tidies sizes, radii, layers and line heights.
